neel: Quick report from an onboarding run: the streaming sample in the notebook can hang on exit if a cell interrupt happens. Observed duplicate last chunk sometimes and TCP stays ESTABLISHED until process exit. :grimacing:

vika: can you paste the tiny repro? SSE/chunked?

neel: SSE-like from `client.stream_text(...)`. Minimal:
```py
async with Client(token=...) as c:
    async for t in c.stream_text(model="sage-7B", prompt="hi"):
        print(t)
```
Interrupt the cell after a few tokens. Last token may print twice and socket not closed.

sam: which sdk/python/aiohttp? any wrappers?

neel: redwood-py 0.9.0, python 3.11.2, aiohttp 3.9.4. no telemetry. Repro also in colab.

vika: quick workaround is explicit iterator close in finally:
```py
it = c.stream_text().__aiter__()
try:
    async for x in it: ...
finally:
    await it.aclose()
```
That closes socket reliably.

neel: works but it's surprising in the quickstart. Also mypy grumbles when storing `it` because of weak iterator typing.

sam: actionable items: 1) make `aclose()` idempotent (no-op on second call) and guard final emit to avoid duplicates; 2) tighten typing so `__aiter__()` returns a generic `AsyncIterator[str]`/StreamIterator[T]; 3) add notebook note about interrupts.

vika: + add a pytest that simulates CancelledError mid-iteration and asserts socket closed and no duplicate final event.

qa-bot: Created issue #4721: "py-sdk streaming: duplicate final chunk + socket leak on interrupt; iterator typing ergonomics" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/issues/4721) :white_check_mark:

neel: thanks — I'll attach the colab and minimal aiohttp server repro. Saves an onboarding faceplant. :sweat_smile:
